headline: OpenAI forked the Git repository on GitHub
summary: The AI research lab has created a fork of the popular distributed version control system, Git, on GitHub.
details: OpenAI, the artificial intelligence research organization, has recently forked the Git repository on GitHub. Git is a widely-used, open-source distributed version control system originally created by Linus Torvalds.

The purpose behind OpenAI forking Git is not immediately clear from the available information. Forks are typically created to experiment with new features, contribute to the original project, or create a derivative project.

Git itself is a foundational tool for software development, enabling collaboration and tracking changes in codebases. Its open-source nature and GNU General Public License v2 allow for widespread use and modification.

The fork was noted on Hacker News, sparking discussion within the developer community about OpenAI's potential intentions with this action. Further details regarding the fork's content or purpose have not been disclosed by OpenAI.

headline_marked: Phoebe Gates' AI Shopping App [[Phia Accused of Fake Clicks]] for Affiliate Sales
headline: Phoebe Gates' AI Shopping App Phia Accused of Fake Clicks for Affiliate Sales
summary: Reports indicate the AI-powered shopping plugin Phia allegedly used cookie stuffing to claim unearned affiliate commissions, with investigations finding fake clicks and misattributed sales.
details: Phoebe Gates, daughter of Bill Gates, co-founded the AI shopping app Phia. Investigations by researchers and platforms like Bloomberg and Capital One Shopping reportedly found that Phia's browser extension engaged in cookie stuffing.

This tactic allegedly involved attaching Phia's affiliate code to sales that were not driven by the app, and even claiming credit for sales that should have gone to other publishers. A researcher detailed how the affiliate link was "invisibly loaded into a second tab" on iOS after visiting a merchant's site.

Phia has attributed the reported issues to a bug in a recent release. A company spokesperson stated that the team worked overnight to resolve the problem after being notified within the last 24 hours.
The feature responsible for these alleged misattributions was reportedly rolled out in December 2025, according to reports from Edelman and Bloomberg.
